name: espn
description: A 10-team ESPN-imported league (platform='espn', espn_auth='public'), so LeagueScreen's ESPN branch — the platform badge, the read-only copy, `league.espn-resync` and the auth-expired variant driven by /__test__/fail_next on /api/espn/import — is reachable for the first time. Also seeds the pick-assignment grid (4 rounds x 4 seasons) WITH a stored order plus 5 recorded picks, which is what makes the ESPN-only pick-assignment and record-picks screens capturable. qa_espn has no Sleeper leagues: the Sleeper league list cassette is [] and the ESPN league arrives through GET /api/espn/leagues, exactly as it does in production. NOTE sleeper.trade_block is pinned OFF: session-init's FB-147 trade-block sync guards on `league_id.isdigit()`, and an ESPN league id IS numeric — so the sync fires against the Sleeper URL space for a league that has none, costing the run a vcr_miss. An ESPN league genuinely has no Sleeper trade block, so off is the honest fixture value; the guard itself wants is_linked_platform_league (server.py already uses that pairing elsewhere). Seeds 1 mutual trade_match + 1 awaiting like IN THE ESPN LEAGUE (audit P0-6, capture request #9 — the highest-leverage single capture in that list): trade_matches is league-scoped with no platform column, and load_matches resolves both partner names from league_members, so an ESPN match renders through the ordinary MatchesScreen path. That is the point — before audit P0-6, SendInSleeperButton returned NULL for a league whose cached platform is 'espn' (#146), so the card showed Dismiss and nothing else with no copy explaining why; it now renders the stated reason plus a 'Copy trade' action, and this profile is the only harness coverage of that branch. CAPTURE PRECONDITION: the button's ESPN test reads useSession().leagues and FAILS OPEN on a league id missing from that cache, so a flow must reach Matches through the league picker (which merges GET /api/espn/leagues) — a direct deep link leaves the cache empty and the Send button WOULD render, capturing the wrong state.
